claims.text: At stage-2 the raw 16 is used both for a screen's padding and for the gap above a button (ProductDetailScreen EdgeInsets.all(16) and SizedBox(height: 16)).
A semantic token is a design token named for where it applies, such as a screen's padding, pointing at a value from a shared scale.

At stage-3 tokens.dart defines Space.sm 8, Space.md 12, Space.lg 16; Insets.screen = EdgeInsets.all(Space.lg), Insets.tile = EdgeInsets.all(Space.md); Sizes.minTapTarget 48 and Sizes.gridRow 72, all static const. EdgeInsets.all(x) gives a padding of x on all four sides.

At stage-3 seven lines in DonHang.App/lib pad with Insets.screen, incl. CreateOrderScreen and ProductDetailScreen. Every screen that pads its content uses Insets.screen, so changing it moves the edge of each of those screens and not the gaps or the tile padding.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: git grep -F Insets.screen -- DonHang.App/lib

claims.text: At stage-3 ProductTile uses Sizes.minTapTarget for its minimum height and Insets.tile for its padding, where stage-2 wrote 48 and 12.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: widgets/product_tile.dart:32,34; @ stage-2: widgets/product_tile.dart (minHeight 48, EdgeInsets.all(12))

claims.text: At stage-3 CreateOrderScreen pads its form with Insets.screen and uses SizedBox(height: Space.lg) and SizedBox(height: Space.sm) around the button; ProductDetailScreen uses Insets.screen and SizedBox(height: Space.lg); neither writes a spacing number.
ProductCatalog lays out the ProductTile rows of the product list: ListView.builder when narrow, GridView.builder when maxWidth >= 600; Sizes.gridRow is the grid's row height (mainAxisExtent).

At stage-3 ProductDetailScreen shows the product name with Theme.of(context).textTheme.headlineSmall, and the error tone of StatusBanner takes its colors from ColorScheme roles (errorContainer, onErrorContainer).
Theme.of(context) returns the ThemeData of the closest Theme above the given context (else the app's theme), so a value read from it follows the light or dark theme in force.

A static const double can be used in a const constructor call such as const SizedBox(height: Space.lg); a value from Theme.of(context) cannot. Flutter advises const widgets where possible: they let Flutter short-circuit most of the rebuild work.
Spacing that is the same in every theme can be plain constants; a value that changes with light and dark belongs in the theme.

When two places share a role through one name, they cannot drift apart by one edited value. A value the designer changes as a whole across screens gets a role name; a gap chosen for one spot on one screen names only its size on the scale.
Tokens belong to a role, not to a screen; per-screen tokens let screens with the same role drift apart again, and a screen that truly differs gets a new role.
git switch --detach <tag> checks out the commit the tag points to with a detached HEAD; grep -rn -F searches recursively for a fixed string and prints line numbers.
claims.source_hint: git-scm docs: git-switch (--detach); GNU grep manual (-r, -n, -F)

claims.text: At stage-3 grep -rn -F "Insets.screen" DonHang.App/lib gives eight matches: seven 'padding: Insets.screen,' lines and the comment on tokens.dart:12.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: git grep -n -F Insets.screen -- DonHang.App/lib

claims.text: Changing Space.lg would also change gaps written as SizedBox(height: Space.lg), such as those on CreateOrderScreen and ProductDetailScreen. A 20 off the scale is EdgeInsets.all(20) (one line) or a new Space step plus Insets.screen built from it (two lines).
